summary: SUPERSEDED — bkit owns the whole region between the FIRST and LAST marker; only bytes above the first and below the last are consumer territory
description: The fold now rewrites the entire generated region in one pass (status block from docs/roadmap.jsonl, tracker block from docs/tracker.jsonl, analysis block carried through verbatim) instead of surgically rewriting one pair at a time. Consumer text above the first marker and below the last is still preserved byte-for-byte; text placed BETWEEN two marker blocks no longer survives a regenerate.
rationale: Writing the region in full is what lets a newly-added marker block appear on an existing consumer board with no upgrade migration — the alternative was a migrateWarningsToNoise-shaped function per new block, forever. The per-pair invariant could not introduce a block at a chosen position: the self-heal path appends a missing pair at EOF, which would have stranded the Tracker block below the consumer Backlog / Ideas region.
alternatives: Per-pair surgical rewrite plus a one-off upgrade migration to insert the tracker pair — REJECTED: a migration per future block. Per-phase marker pairs (bkit:design/bkit:plan/...) to make parsing collision-proof — REJECTED: solved a parsing problem that disappeared once the status block stopped being parsed back at all.

summary: SUPERSEDED — no phase close reads the tracker at all; the read lives only in /bkit-roadmap
description: Ship close carried a list_issues tracker enrichment so a full-regenerate fold would not blank tracker-only board rows. Both halves of that reasoning are gone: tracker issues render in their own marker block from docs/tracker.jsonl, so the status block a close re-renders holds nothing but ledger rows and there is nothing to blank. All five closes now fold from the ledger and issue no tracker read. The reverse label-sync moved out of ship for the same reason.
rationale: A workflow running on one issue may mutate only that issue. A tracker read touches every open issue and the reverse label-sync writes labels on issues other than the one in hand, so both belong to the one command whose job is the whole board.
alternatives: Keep enrichment at every close — REJECTED: a full-board rewrite of every open issue on a per-issue workflow. Keep it at ship only — REJECTED: same rule violation, and ship is not privileged.

summary: docs/tracker.jsonl is a gitignored snapshot rewritten in full each run, not an append-only ledger
description: kind:"tracker" rows mirror every open tracker issue (title, description, metadata; comments only for the shortlist). The file is overwritten every /bkit-roadmap run, one row per issue, and is gitignored.
rationale: Every other jsonl ledger records something with no home outside the repo; tracker content is authoritative in the tracker. Rebuilding from scratch removes the whole cache-invalidation class — no since filter, no local timestamp diff, no periodic resync, and a deleted issue or comment cannot go stale. Gitignoring keeps ~1.7MB of third-party comment text out of git history and out of a consumer repo.
alternatives: Tracked and append-only like docs/roadmap.jsonl — REJECTED: stores a full copy of an issue body and comments on every edit, worst on the issues touched most, and commits other people's comment text. Incremental since-based sync — REJECTED as unnecessary once the sync dropped comments and became 2 calls on github, 1 on linear.

summary: The analysis runs in two passes — a shortlist agent picks what to read in full, then the ranking agent reads only that
description: @bkit-roadmap-shortlist selects at most bkit.roadmap.shortlistSize (default 10) items from a cheap jq index over docs/tracker.jsonl; the orchestrator fetches comments for those only; @bkit-roadmap-refresh ranks with their full text. ROADMAP_SCAN_COVERAGE reports items read in full over every open issue plus the ledger frontier. Ranking is severity-first: security, then errors and correctness, then user-facing impact.
rationale: Reading every open issue is not a trade-off but impossible — measured at 416k tokens against a 200k context on a 68-issue repo — and mechanical trimming does not rescue it (code fences 4%, plus blockquotes 5%). The leaf holds no MCP tools and linear has no CLI, so enrichment must be orchestrator-mediated, which forces two passes. Severity ordering is derived from issue content so it still works where there is no state axis and no priority field at all.
alternatives: Cached per-issue digest written by a cheap model, invalidated on updatedAt — REJECTED as unnecessary machinery once the shortlist is agent-chosen. Bodies-only for all issues — REJECTED: discards every comment, and comments are 78% of the content. Per-issue hard character cap — REJECTED: truncates mid-sentence and favours whatever was written first.

summary: Claude sessions stay in acceptEdits with workspace trust granted host-side and no ask row on shell curl/wget — the only combination that reaches zero permission prompts without putting a classifier in the loop
description: Three levers decide how often a Claude session stops to ask, and only one combination reaches zero. (1) defaultMode stays acceptEdits: it is the one value of the three that actually takes effect from .claude/settings.json, and it leaves the blanket Bash(*) allow in force. (2) Workspace trust is granted host-side by the generated cloud setup script, without which every allow row is ignored and each Bash call prompts. (3) Shell curl and wget carry no ask row, because a content-scoped ask is evaluated before the auto-mode classifier and always forces a prompt that a cloud session cannot answer. Destructive-git and .env-read ask rows are deliberately kept: every destructive-git command is already on the PROHIBITED list in all five workflow headers, so none fires in normal operation and they cost no friction.
rationale: The goal is the fewest interruptions per workflow run, with mistakes absorbed by git rather than by prompts. acceptEdits plus trust plus no network ask row produces no prompts and no classifier round-trip on any command. The kept rows guard the one class git cannot undo: untracked files and uncommitted work have no reflog, so git clean -fd and git checkout -- . are unrecoverable in a way a bad commit never is. Claude cannot express a per-domain curl allow at all — its rules match a command prefix, not a URL host — so blanket-allow was the only alternative to a prompt on every fetch.
alternatives: Switch defaultMode to auto — REJECTED, and it does not work where it would be set: auto has no effect from .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json (it also suppresses a user-scope defaultMode), and even applied from user settings it is higher friction, not lower, because auto mode drops blanket Bash(*) and routes every shell command through the classifier, adding a round-trip per command, classifier blocks as a new failure mode, and a fallback to prompting after three consecutive blocks. Keep the curl/wget ask rows and ratify them into the parity suite — REJECTED: one guaranteed prompt per context=web context-fetch block, unanswerable in cloud. Port Cursor's URL-host-parsing guardrail to Claude and opencode — the correct fix for the remaining edge (an undeclared host is ungated on Claude) but a materially larger build; left open on 441.

summary: Three consumer Notes blocks in docs/roadmap.md are carried through every fold and never overwritten
description: docs/roadmap.md carries three <!-- bkit:roadmap-notes-{pre,mid,post} --> marker pairs: above the bkit list, between bkit and tracker, and below the tracker list. bkit_roadmap_fold extracts each body and re-emits it unchanged; a missing pair is seeded with a placeholder. Analysis, head, and Backlog stay on their existing preserve paths.
rationale: Users need durable free-form notes next to the generated lists. Head and Backlog cannot sit between those lists, and rewriting the whole generated region would wipe anything written there.
alternatives: Preserve unnamed gaps between generated marker pairs — REJECTED: the fold rewrites the region in full so a new mechanical block can be introduced without a migration, and unnamed gaps have no owner. Sidecar notes file — REJECTED: notes belong next to the lists they annotate.

summary: docs/roadmap.md notes-post is last and replaces ## Backlog / Ideas
description: bkit_roadmap_fold writes roadmap-notes-post after roadmap-analysis as the last block. The default ## Backlog / Ideas seed is not emitted. A legacy Backlog heading plus its default italic is stripped; remaining consumer tail and adopted/mangled boards merge into notes-post.
rationale: The post-list Notes block is the consumer-owned end of the board. A sibling Backlog heading after analysis was a second last region that fold kept reseeding.
alternatives: Keep both Backlog and notes-post — REJECTED: notes-post goes last and replaces Backlog. Keep Backlog after analysis with notes-post still below tracker — REJECTED: that leaves two consumer tails.

summary: The three tracker-carried bkit markers are h6 headings; detection is whole-line and reads either syntax
description: bkit:generated, bkit:ignore-earlier and bkit:blocked-by move from the HTML-comment form to `###### bkit:{name}`. Detection matches a WHOLE LINE in either syntax, so markers already written into an issue keep working and only the heading form is emitted. File-only markers (bkit:start/end, bkit:roadmap-*, bkit:tracker {name} start) are unchanged: they never cross a tracker API.
rationale: mcp__github__issue_read deletes every HTML comment from a body, so an HTML-comment marker could never survive a read — recorded in docs/knowledge.jsonl under github-mcp-issue-read-sanitises-bodies-killing-every-html-comment-marker, which also observed that a sanitised read begins at the comment's FIRST HEADING. A heading is therefore the one form with evidence of surviving. Whole-line detection is what lets the guard test narrow: an inline mention of a token in prose or a prompt is no longer a live marker, so describing the mechanism no longer arms it. The blocked-by encode is the case where sanitisation cost real data rather than a silent no-op, because design reads the body and writes it back. The raw gh api mandate STAYS until a live MCP round trip confirms the heading returns intact; the GitHub MCP server was returning 400 when this landed.
alternatives: Keep HTML comments and mandate raw gh api forever — REJECTED: makes the read path load-bearing on every future caller and is what blocks a bulk MCP tracker read. Backtick-escape the marker — REJECTED, already measured: the sanitiser runs on raw markdown and returns empty backticks. Emit heading form only with no legacy read — REJECTED: silently drops every human-placed cut and every generated stamp already in the tracker. Infer bkit-ness from template heading shape — REJECTED previously and still: needs lockstep maintenance with every template heading and eats human comments sharing a heading.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the board carries two Notes blocks, not three, and renders no tracker table
description: The fold still rewrites the whole generated region in one pass, but the region is now Notes / roadmap-status / roadmap-analysis / Notes. The roadmap-notes-mid pair is deleted along with the tracker block it used to sit beside. Consumer text above the first marker and below the last is still preserved byte-for-byte.
rationale: notes-mid existed only to give the consumer somewhere to write between the bkit list and the tracker list. With no tracker list it has nothing to sit between.

summary: SUPERSEDED — there is no tracker snapshot; docs/tracker.jsonl and the kind:"tracker" row shape are deleted
description: bkit no longer copies the tracker anywhere. The sync step, the snapshot file, its gitignore entry, the tracker marker block and the tracker row shape in .bkit/jsonl.md are all removed.
rationale: docs/roadmap.md renders only what has no other home. A wired tracker already shows its own issues and its own closures, so a regenerated copy is a second source that can only go stale. Open tracker issues reach the board through the analysis block as ranked recommendations, never as a mechanical table.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the shortlist is human-chosen from the Notes blocks, not agent-chosen from a jq index
description: @bkit-roadmap-shortlist is deleted. Full reads go to what the human named in the docs/roadmap.md Notes blocks and to the open rows of the bkit block; every other open tracker issue is read title, description and metadata only, with no comments. Shipped rows are not read in full.
rationale: The token measurement that forced two passes still holds — comments are 78% of the content — but the person who knows which issues matter this week is the person writing the Notes. The shortlist agent was a model guessing at something a human already knows.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the legacy Backlog strip is gone; consumer text is preserved verbatim and never special-cased
description: notes-post is still last, but _bkit_roadmap_strip_legacy_backlog is deleted. A `## Backlog / Ideas` heading in a consumer's board is now carried into notes-post like any other consumer text rather than being recognised and dropped.
rationale: The Backlog seed only ever shipped on dev, so no consumer has one to migrate. A fold that recognises and deletes a specific heading is a rule that can only fire on text bkit itself wrote, and preserving every byte is the simpler contract.

summary: SUPERSEDED — no close reads the tracker because nothing on the board comes from the tracker
description: The ship-close drift check and bkit-roadmap-reconcile.sh are deleted along with the cadence evaluator. Every phase close does one thing: append its feature row and re-render the roadmap-status block from the ledger.
rationale: The question of whether a close should enrich from the tracker disappears once the board holds no tracker-derived rows to enrich.

summary: BAR-141 — Structured PreflightFinding replaces printSink
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Replace `ModuleContext.printSink: string[]` with `ModuleContext.advisories: PreflightFinding[]` (shape: `{id, severity, detect, action}`). Install restructured into three phases: Phase 1 preflight (read-only, blockers short-circuit before any writes), Phase 2 dispatch (unchanged), Phase 3 post-install re-detection (token surfaces, ci.yml, vale sync, devDeps). Findings deduplicated by `id` — Phase 3 wins on conflict.
- **Why:** `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep `printSink` + add parallel `findings: PreflightFinding[]` — two sinks → drift risk; downstream tooling has to merge two shapes. (2) `--strict` flag promoting advisories to blockers — out of scope; consumer can use `bkit check` (exit-1-on-drift). (3) Auto-apply advisory fixes — violates consumer-value-wins principle.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, `docs/plans/202605/bar-141-preflight-checklist-plan.md`, `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`, DE-3, KN-4
rationale: `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).

summary: BAR-139 — .bkit-version schema extension: tier3Hashes
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Extend `.bkit/version` from a plain-text semver pin to a JSON object `{ pinnedVersion: string; tier3Hashes: Record<path, sha256> }`. The sha256 map records the content hash of each Tier-3 file at install time. During `bkit uninstall`, `shouldDeleteTier3` checks whether current on-disk content matches the recorded hash — if so, safe to delete; if not (consumer modified), preserved. Backward-compat reader parses old plain-text payloads as `{ pinnedVersion, tier3Hashes: {} }` (unknown → preserve-default).
- **Why:** Tier-3 files (seed-or-print) are deleted during uninstall only if still in the exact state bkit wrote them. Without a recorded hash, `bkit uninstall` cannot distinguish a default-seeded `ci.yml` (safe to delete) from a consumer-customised one (must preserve). Plain-text format is insufficient; JSON is human-readable and extensible.
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep plain-text; detect "default content" by re-rendering the template at uninstall time — fails for Tier-3 files with token substitution bkit can no longer re-compute (consumer tokens may have changed). (2) Store hashes in a separate `.bkit-hashes.json` — two files to keep in sync; `.bkit-version` is the natural home.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-139, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts`
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** The version file also carries an additive `webFetchDerived` field (`.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`).
rationale: Tier-3 files (seed-or-print) are deleted during uninstall only if still in the exact state bkit wrote them. Without a recorded hash, `bkit uninstall` cannot distinguish a default-seeded `ci.yml` (safe to delete) from a consumer-customised one (must preserve). Plain-text format is insufficient; JSON is human-readable and extensible.

summary: BAR-142 §A2 — .bkitignore public contract
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** `.bkitignore` is a new public file at the consumer repo root. Syntax: `#` comment, blank-line ignore, [picomatch](https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch) glob, optional `:dotted.key` suffix for per-key exclusion. Per-key is opt-in behind `BKIT_BKITIGNORE_PER_KEY=1` env var (off by default). Once shipped, the file and its syntax are a public contract.
- **Why:** Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.
- **Discarded:** (1) Make per-key the default — implementation cost likely high; opt-in via env covers the primary use case. (2) Use a custom DSL instead of gitignore-style — picomatch is well-understood, has no shell-out, and is a pure-regex library (security: no injection risk). (3) Store in `.agents/.bkitignore` — consumer-owned files belong at repo root, not in the `.agents/` subtree (which is bkit-managed).
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A2, `.bkit/src/bkit-bkitignore.ts`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl` (per-key deferred)
rationale: Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.

summary: BAR-142 §A5 — `bkit upgrade` diff engine + `canonicalHashes`
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** (1) `canonicalHashes` is an additive field in `.bkit/version` (v0.9.x+): map of consumer-relative path → sha256 of bkit-written content at install time. (2) `bkit upgrade` uses `isConsumerModified(relPath, absPath, canonicalHashes)` to detect consumer drift: if disk hash ≠ canonical hash → conflict, do NOT overwrite. (3) `--non-interactive`: auto-apply non-conflicting; emit conflict list to stderr; exit non-zero on any conflict. (4) `updateCanonicalHashesAfterUpgrade` updates hashes for upgraded files post-run.
- **Why:** Silent overwrite of consumer drift was the root cause of the Gether regression (KN-8). `canonicalHashes` gives the upgrade engine a per-file ownership record that survives across installs. Backward-compat: absent field → `{}` → all files appear "unknown" → conservative no-overwrite (safe).
- **Discarded:** (1) Three-way merge UI — OOS per plan. (2) Timestamp-based drift detection — unreliable across CI environments (git checkout resets mtime). (3) Storing full file content in `.bkit-version` — too large; sha256 is sufficient for drift detection.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A5, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.test.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.integration.test.ts`, KN-8
rationale: Silent overwrite of consumer drift was the root cause of the Gether regression (KN-8). `canonicalHashes` gives the upgrade engine a per-file ownership record that survives across installs. Backward-compat: absent field → `{}` → all files appear "unknown" → conservative no-overwrite (safe).

summary: BAR-131 follow-up — `isConsumerModified` defaults missing canonical hash to drift
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Flip `isConsumerModified`'s default for unknown files: when `canonicalHashes` has no entry for `relPath`, return `true` (treat as modified) rather than `false`. `bkit upgrade`'s `diffFile` adds an idempotent `disk == template → skip` check before the drift branch so identical files are not flagged as spurious conflicts. Existing pre-v0.9.x consumers (or any managed file installed before BAR-142 introduced `canonicalHashes`) will see all-conflict on first `bkit upgrade` and must resolve each manually — this is the safe failure mode.
- **Why:** DE-10 stated the intent as "absent field → conservative no-overwrite (safe)" but the implementation returned `false` from `isConsumerModified` for unknown files, which `bkit upgrade` interpreted as "no drift → safe to overwrite". The result was the opposite of conservative: any managed file lacking a recorded canonical hash was silently overwritten with the current template. Verified during the v1.0.0 ship cycle when running `bkit upgrade` on the bkit repo itself queued a 700-line wipe across `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/knowledge.md`, and others — none of which had recorded hashes because they had not been re-written by `bkit install` since the BAR-142 schema landed.
- **Discarded:** (1) Have `bkit install` retroactively populate `canonicalHashes` for every managed file (not just files in `ws.writes`) — larger surface change; can be added later as an opt-in `bkit install --reseed-hashes` flag. (2) Add a CLI prompt for unknown-hash files — `--non-interactive` flow has no human; conflict-by-default is the only honest answer there.
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** DE-10, BAR-131, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts:168-181`, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts:79-116`, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.test.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.test.ts`, commit 954e827
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** `isConsumerModified` is `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts:182-194`; the unknown-hash -> `true` default holds (`:191`). Line anchors in the text above are pre-move.
rationale: DE-10 stated the intent as "absent field → conservative no-overwrite (safe)" but the implementation returned `false` from `isConsumerModified` for unknown files, which `bkit upgrade` interpreted as "no drift → safe to overwrite". The result was the opposite of conservative: any managed file lacking a recorded canonical hash was silently overwritten with the current template. Verified during the v1.0.0 ship cycle when running `bkit upgrade` on the bkit repo itself queued a 700-line wipe across `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/knowledge.md`, and others — none of which had recorded hashes because they had not been re-written by `bkit install` since the BAR-142 schema landed.

summary: BAR-131 follow-up — auto-seed `canonicalHashes` for `bkit upgrade` skipped files
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Extend `updateCanonicalHashesAfterUpgrade` to record canonical hashes for files classified as `skip` by `diffFile` (where `disk == template`), in addition to the existing `update` path. Conflict files are explicitly NOT seeded — that would re-introduce the silent-overwrite bug DE-12 fixed. The install-side caller in `bkit-install.ts` was widened to invoke the function whenever `updated.length > 0 || skipped.length > 0`. After v1.0.1 ships, consumers running `bkit upgrade` once auto-heal the missing-hash gap; truly-customised files continue to surface as conflicts requiring manual resolution.
- **Why:** DE-12 made `bkit upgrade` safe-by-default but left every file without a recorded canonical hash flagging as a conflict on first run — including files that exactly match the template. For pre-v0.9.x consumers (or any repo where bkit-managed files had not been re-written by `bkit install` since BAR-142), this meant an all-conflict first upgrade. Reseeding only on confirmed `disk == template` matches is provably safe — the canonical hash equals the template hash by definition — and lets the engine distinguish true drift from no-drift on the next run. Verified locally: bkit repo `.bkit-version` `canonicalHashes` grew from 4 → 31 entries after one `bkit upgrade` run; 17 genuinely-customised files remain as conflicts.
- **Discarded:** (1) Auto-seed during `bkit install` (the option mentioned in DE-12) — install does not call `runUpgrade`, so adding it would require duplicating the candidate-enumeration logic. The upgrade-side fix covers the same consumer migration with less surface area. (2) Seed all bkit-managed files with current disk hash — re-introduces the silent-overwrite bug for any customised file (canonical=disk implies "no drift" on next upgrade, which then auto-overwrites with the new template).
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** DE-12, BAR-131, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts:209-249`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:803-810`, `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.test.ts`, commits e2889e1 (feature) + 20d63d6 (seeded `.bkit-version`)
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** `updateCanonicalHashesAfterUpgrade` is `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts:465` and seeds `updated` + `skipped`. The install-side caller (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:2777`) runs on every non-dry-run upgrade; it is no longer guarded on `updated.length > 0 || skipped.length > 0`.
rationale: DE-12 made `bkit upgrade` safe-by-default but left every file without a recorded canonical hash flagging as a conflict on first run — including files that exactly match the template. For pre-v0.9.x consumers (or any repo where bkit-managed files had not been re-written by `bkit install` since BAR-142), this meant an all-conflict first upgrade. Reseeding only on confirmed `disk == template` matches is provably safe — the canonical hash equals the template hash by definition — and lets the engine distinguish true drift from no-drift on the next run. Verified locally: bkit repo `.bkit-version` `canonicalHashes` grew from 4 → 31 entries after one `bkit upgrade` run; 17 genuinely-customised files remain as conflicts.

summary: BAR-169 — Tiered rebase-conflict auto-recovery
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Three-tier conflict handling across all three orchestrator workflows (`bkit-ship`, `bkit-build`, `bkit-debug`):
  (a) **Append-only doc ledgers** (`docs/deferrals.jsonl`, `docs/knowledge.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/completed.md`) → `merge=union` declared in `.gitattributes` (template at `.bkit/templates/.gitattributes`, installed to consumer roots via `bkit install`). Git auto-concatenates both sides at rebase/merge time; conflict never reaches the workflow.
  (b) **Lockfile (`pnpm-lock.yaml`)** → inline retry in Step 2 of all three workflows: `git checkout --theirs` + `pnpm install --lockfile-only` + `git add` + `rebase --continue`.
  (c) **Code / configs / everything else** → sentinel-file Failure Path. Ship's Failure Path additionally invokes `@bkit-ship-conflict-resolve` (mechanical-only, narrow-scope subagent) before `@bkit-debug-abort-handover` to catch non-overlapping additive edits / formatting drift / dep-version supersedes; on `Verdict: PASS` workflow resumes, on `FAIL`/`CONCERNS` falls through to handover. Build/debug do NOT get the resolver subagent — their conflicts usually point to a deeper problem worth a human glance.
- **Why:** Pre-fix shape was `git rebase || exit 1` in all three workflows — every conflict (additive or semantic) routed to the same dead-end abort. PR #17 (BAR-155) hit a single additive `docs/deferrals.jsonl` conflict that bkit could not auto-recover, requiring manual resolution and CI re-trigger. Tiering by conflict shape lets the cheap mechanical cases self-heal while preserving human review on genuinely ambiguous code conflicts. Trade-off accepted: `merge=union` will silently produce duplicate `KN-N` / `DE-N` IDs if both branches allocate the same number — same renumbering hazard already deferred separately, not a regression introduced here.
- **Discarded:** (1) Single uniform sentinel→handover path for all conflicts — preserves current dead-end. (2) New full workflow Step for conflict resolution — adds status.json/gate/comment overhead for what is mechanical recovery; better as inline sub-step of Step 2. (3) Repurpose `bkit-debug` workflow for rebase conflicts — its diagnose/remediate subagents are scoped to test failures; verdict signal "tests pass" is necessary but not sufficient for a merge (tests can pass while one side's intent is silently dropped). (4) Wire `bkit-ship-conflict-resolve` into build/debug Failure Paths — those workflows operate on the feature branch in isolation; conflicts there are rarer and usually indicate deeper problems. (5) `.agents/friction.md` for `merge=union` — friction.md has post-write edits to `Recovery`/`Status` fields, breaking the strict-append contract that union-safety requires.
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** BAR-169, BAR-155, PR #17, `.bkit/templates/.gitattributes`, `.gitattributes`, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md` Step 2, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md` Step 2, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md` Step 2, `.bkit/prompts/bkit-ship-conflict-resolve.md`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts` (`NPM_STRIP_REMAP`)
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** Tier (a) union set is the JSONL ledgers, not the old `.md` files: `docs/knowledge.jsonl`, `docs/decisions.jsonl`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl`, `docs/failures.jsonl`, `.bkit/issues.jsonl`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `.bkit/stats.jsonl`, `docs/plans/**/status.jsonl` (`.gitattributes`). This repo also sets `merge=union` on `.bkit/friction.jsonl`, so discarded item (5) no longer applies. Tier (b) lives in `.bkit/scripts/bkit-rebase-resolve.sh`, sourced by `/bkit-design`, `/bkit-plan`, `/bkit-build` and `/bkit-debug` (not `/bkit-ship`). Tier (c) `@bkit-ship-conflict-resolve` and `NPM_STRIP_REMAP` hold.
rationale: Pre-fix shape was `git rebase || exit 1` in all three workflows — every conflict (additive or semantic) routed to the same dead-end abort. PR #17 (BAR-155) hit a single additive `docs/deferrals.jsonl` conflict that bkit could not auto-recover, requiring manual resolution and CI re-trigger. Tiering by conflict shape lets the cheap mechanical cases self-heal while preserving human review on genuinely ambiguous code conflicts. Trade-off accepted: `merge=union` will silently produce duplicate `KN-N` / `DE-N` IDs if both branches allocate the same number — same renumbering hazard already deferred separately, not a regression introduced here.

summary: BAR-167 — Drop `__bkit__` envelope; adopt deep-containment ownership model
rationale: The `__bkit__` envelope caused two real-world failure modes on 2026-05-09 consumer audit: (1) duplicate content — the same hook block appeared inside `__bkit__` AND at the top level, causing confusion and bloat; (2) silent drift — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lost its `pnpm bkit check` step with no detection. The envelope model required consumers to hold two copies of every bkit-owned key. Deep-containment eliminates the duplication: the template IS the declared scope; the consumer only needs to contain it. Consumer-added keys outside the template tree are never touched. `writeTier2Json` THROW (envelope guard) was a footgun — deep-containment removes the need for it entirely.

summary: #160 — `.bkit/` is the install source of truth; `.agents/` is bkit's own runtime
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Centralise all install-related code and payload under a new `.bkit/` root. Engine `.bkit/src/bkit-*.ts` → `.bkit/src/`; install payload `.bkit/templates/**` (incl. `.claude`/`.cursor`/`.github`/`.husky`/root dotfiles) → `.bkit/templates/**`. bkit's **own** runtime `.agents/` content (workflows, prompts, rules, docs, skills) **stays** in `.agents/` — it is dogfooded content an installed consumer also has, not install machinery. Source lookups funnel through one seam in `bkit-paths.ts`: `getTemplatesRoot()` (only place `.bkit/templates` is encoded), `getPkgRoot()` suffix extended from `.agents/scripts` to `.bkit/src`, new `isDogfood()` (`getPkgRoot() === process.cwd()`). `tsconfig` `rootDir`/`include` → `.bkit/src`; `outDir: dist` and `bin: ./dist/bkit-install.js` **unchanged** (`dist/` stays flat at repo root). `files[]` adds `.bkit`, drops `.agents` as install source. `NPM_STRIP_REMAP` (`gitignore`→`.gitignore`) unchanged, applies under `.bkit/templates/`. The `runPayload` templates arm is deleted (dead after move); the workflow/prompt arm keeps its `src === dst` dogfood no-op unchanged. No `.bkit-version` schema or consumer migration. Ships big-bang in one release, gated by a pre-refactor `.bkit-version` hash baseline + dry-run-parity check verifying byte-identical install AND upgrade on a packed tarball in a clean dir.
- **Why:** `.agents/` was three things at once (engine host, install source, bkit's own runtime), so the cross-agent/IDE files (`.claude`/`.cursor`/`.github`/`.husky`) sat mislocated under `.bkit/templates/`. Drawing one line — "source of truth for what bkit ships" (`.bkit/`) vs "bkit's own working files" (`.agents/`) — makes the model honest and keeps "bkit's `.agents/` == a consumer's `.agents/`" for dogfooding. A single resolver seam makes the move auditable and 3am-diagnosable. The hash baseline makes a big-bang move safe without a staged fallback window.
- **Discarded:** (1) Two-release staged migration (alias-first then drop fallback) — its dual-ship safety net is made redundant by the hash oracle and it adds a dual-tree-divergence risk + permanent fallback resolver fork. (2) Full mirror moving workflows/prompts/rules under `.bkit/templates/` too — breaks the workflow/prompt `src === dst` no-op, turns bkit's own workflows into silently-reverting generated files, risks non-byte-identical self-install. (3) Engine-only lift (templates stay) — incomplete-refactor trap; adds a third location, leaves the headline mislocation untouched. summary: #274 — GH Packages auth moves to pnpm user-level config; Vercel `installCommand` shim is not a DE-3/BAR-164 regression
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** The `@cbartens/bkit` registry auth token no longer lives in the committed project `.npmrc` (which now carries ONLY `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`). It is written into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install`: CI (a step before install), local dev (run once), and Vercel (via a `vercel.json` `installCommand: pnpm config set //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL && pnpm install`).
- **Why:** pnpm's auth-handling rework (regression boundary between 10.34.1 and 10.34.3, confirmed live) stopped honouring a project-`.npmrc` `${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` env-substitution at install fetch time — `pnpm install`/`add` 401s (`ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401`) even with the token set (metadata `pnpm view` still resolves, masking it). Config precedence (project `.npmrc` > user config) means a leftover project auth line would also shadow the user-level token, so the token must be _relocated_, not duplicated. `pnpm config set` is version-aware — it writes `~/.npmrc` on pnpm 10.x and `~/.config/pnpm/auth.ini` on pnpm 11.x — so the same command is correct across pnpm majors (preferred over a hand-written `~/.npmrc`). Unblocks #273 (pnpm 10.34.3) and the pnpm-11 migration (#176).
- **Not a regression of DE-3 / DE-11(BAR-164):** DE-3 removed a _git-auth_ installCommand (`git config --global url."…x-access-token…".insteadOf`), obsolete once bkit left git-dep — no git ceremony returns here. The new Vercel `installCommand` is a minimal registry-auth shim required only because the env-substitution path DE-3 leaned on broke.
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep the project `.npmrc` `_authToken` line as belt-and-suspenders — rejected: it shadows the user-level token and still 401s. (2) Hand-write `~/.npmrc` in CI — rejected: misses pnpm 11's `auth.ini`. (3) Pin Vercel to pnpm <10.34.3 — rejected: fragile (Vercel auto-bumps pnpm).

summary: #261 — CI-Dispatch Gate: outcome-based verification of the final loud push (4-outcome state machine; post-final-push only; 2 sites not 3; ship out)
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Replace the pre-push HEAD-subject string clause (§ "HEAD-Subject Assertion", #184) with a two-part **CI-Dispatch Gate**: (1) retain the deny-list pre-push fast-fail as-is; (2) add a post-push outcome poll that confirms a `bkit-tests-scope` run appears in `statusCheckRollup` for the exact pushed HEAD, self-heals once with a clean `re-trigger` commit if none appears, and terminates with a named 4-outcome verdict: `dispatched` / `self-healed` / `no-ci` / `unresolved`. The gate fires post-final-push only (build Gate 18, debug Gate 10). Sub-reason codes: `timeout-dirty` / `retrigger-suppressed` / `autoroute-mismatch` / `gh-error`. Named symbols: `POLL_BUDGET_S=60`, `POLL_INTERVAL_S=10`, `[bkit-ci-gate]` log prefix. Verdict written to `step-done.ciDispatch` (additive NDJSON field, backward-compatible with #209 FOLD). Two companion guards: EC-1 pre-flight at build Step 17 (detect existing open PR before blind `gh pr create`); EC-2 abort-guard at build inline Failure Path + shared § Failure Path step 5 (preserve last validated remote HEAD — do NOT push `[skip ci]` abort commit onto a live PR).
- **Why:** The pre-push string clause only checks the orchestrator's own commit (clean by construction) and never confirms a run was actually dispatched — any mid-run interruption leaving a `[skip ci]` HEAD as the remote HEAD silently empties the PR's `statusCheckRollup` and admits a vacuously green PR to ship (KN-11). The most likely path (EC-2: Failure Path pushes a `[skip ci]` abort commit onto a branch with an existing open PR) was completely unguarded. Outcome verification closes both the detection gap and the abuse path.
- **D2 preserved:** `[skip ci]` on `worktree-setup` / `create-pr` commits is load-bearing (KN-30 / §141 D2/D3 cloud auto-route concurrency design). The gate fires post-final-push only — zero additional mid-build CI triggers. The re-trigger commit carries the same `AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX` as the close-workflow commit so the cloud auto-router sees a consistent marker.
- **`retrigger-suppressed` → `unresolved` (never `no-ci`):** if the re-trigger commit itself carries a suppressor, the gate cannot discriminate "no CI workflow for this event" from "CI suppressed by token in re-trigger HEAD" — mapping to `no-ci` would give a false logged-pass. The only safe outcome is `unresolved` (Failure Path) which surfaces the suppression for human inspection.
- **`bkit-tests-scope` fuzzy match:** `test("decide"; "i")` case-insensitive probe, not an exact literal name match. Consumer-renamed `bkit-tests-scope` would otherwise produce a permanent self-heal → `no-ci` / `unresolved` cycle. The same tolerance as ship's existing `test("test"; "i")` probe.
- **Discarded — 3 sites (add gate at ship):** Ship already has a `SQUASH_SHA`-poll gate at Step 13. Adding a CI-Dispatch self-heal at ship would mask the #81 Change C "essential tests skipped" signal — ship is the designed downstream backstop, not a self-healer.
- **Discarded — whole-gate byte-equality (build ≡ debug):** The two gate sites legitimately differ in AUTO_ROUTE sourcing (build re-derives from `LABELS` in-block; debug reads `BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE` before `rm`). WS-6 asserts equality only on the SHARED poll-loop + named-symbol sub-lines.
- **Discarded — EC-1 mid-build PR-mode push:** A mid-build `synchronize` on a clean HEAD is exactly the D2 auto-router defect. EC-1 is a pre-flight fail-fast (detect existing PR → Failure Path with named message), not a mid-build push.
- **Discarded — `PUSH_MODE`-based no-op for "no CI":** LOCAL mode still dispatches CI (it creates a PR). The only legitimate no-op is "no CI workflow for this event," discriminated by the clean re-trigger dispatching nothing.
- **Source:** phase
